children: Regulators are reining in a wild corner of prediction markets where traders bet on which words will be spoken by politicians, executives and celebrities, saying that so-called "mention markets" are vulnerable to abuse.
Mention markets "may present a heightened risk of susceptibility to manipulation," the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said in an advisory yesterday.
Last month, the CFTC fined President Trump's former teleprompter operator for using his advance access to the president's speeches to make profitable bets on Trump mention markets on Kalshi.

In Tuesday's advisory, the CFTC noted that mention markets differ from other wagers offered by platforms like Kalshi, such as election bets, because the outcome of a mention bet depends on the actions of a single individual-the speaker whose words are being bet on. That could make it possible for bad actors to pressure the speaker to say certain words, swinging the outcome, according to the CFTC.

The advisory doesn't ban mention trading altogether. But the CFTC is makes it harder for prediction markets to offer such bets, by pushing them to prove that their planned contracts can't easily be manipulated.
For more on why critics have been calling for tighter regulation of mentions markets, check out this story I worked on earlier this year about the traders who bet on Trump speeches.
